study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modelling of brain function abnormalities in complex pathology needs the whole brain

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: The study introduces a novel whole-brain normative modeling approach for functional connectivity (FUNCOIN) to capture system-level deviations. It aims to demonstrate that this integrative method is more suitable for identifying individuals with complex conditions like bipolar disorder and Parkinson's disease compared to localized (edgewise) approaches.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly states the use of the UK Biobank (UKB) dataset for the healthy/normative cohort throughout the manuscript.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Using FUNCOIN and UK Biobank resting-state fMRI data from 46,000 healthy subjects across training and testing sets...

rci2_hc_n.reason: The paper specifies that the healthy cohort was split into a training set of 32,000 subjects and a test set of 14,000 subjects. The total is 32,000 + 14,000 = 46,000.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: We divide the subjects into three groups: A large group of healthy subjects to train the model on (training data, N =32,000), a set of healthy subjects on which we test the out-of-sample performance of the model (test data, N =14,000), and a group of subjects with psychiatric or neurological diagnoses.
rci2_hc_n.location: Kobbersmed2025.pdf.md: Results / Whole-brain normative modelling of FC

rci3_hc_age.supporting_text: The age variable was linearly transformed the interval [0,1], with 0 and 1 corresponding to the minimum and maximum age in the whole dataset (44.56 and 85.43 years).

rci5_imaging_modality.reason: The paper consistently and explicitly states that resting-state fMRI (rsfMRI) data from the UK Biobank was used for the analysis.
rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: Using FUNCOIN and UK Biobank resting-state fMRI data from 46,000 healthy subjects across training and testing sets, we found that subjects with bipolar disorder and Parkinson's disease were significantly, and substantially, more likely than healthy subjects to exhibit abnormal FC patterns, which was not seen in localized models.

rci6_analysis_level.supporting_text: FUNCOIN, which we released in a Python package, finds FC components (i.e. linear projections) that are maximally related to sex and age (or other specified covariates)...

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: UKB ICA parcellation (55 components); removal of first 8 time points.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The paper states that the UKB's 55-component ICA parcellation was used. It also mentions a specific step of removing the first 8 time points. However, it refers to previous UKB papers for the full details of the main preprocessing pipeline.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: We used the UKB ICA parcellation with 55 ICA components... Details on data acquisition and preprocessing can be found in previous UKB papers... We therefore right-truncated all time series to 490 points followed by removal of the first 8 time points.

rci8_quality_checking.detail: The paper does not describe any specific quality control procedures applied by the authors beyond what was presumably performed in the standard UKB processing pipeline, which is cited but not detailed. The only data cleaning step mentioned is the truncation of time points. -
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: Details on data acquisition and preprocessing can be found in previous UKB papers...

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: The authors investigated potential scanning site effects but found none on the Z-scores of healthy subjects. Consequently, site was not included as a covariate in the final reported model. -
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: In line with earlier normative modelling studies on structural MRI from UKB, we found no scanning site effects on the Z-scores of the healthy subjects (see Supplementary text and Supplementary Fig. 6).

nm1_model_origin.detail: The paper introduces FUNCOIN as a 'novel' method developed for this study. It is not a pre-trained model. -
nm1_model_origin.supporting_text: To fill this gap, we introduce Functional Connectivity Integrative Normative Modelling (FUNCOIN) as a method to evaluate how pathology pushes individuals from the normative range of brain function at a system level.

nm2_modeling_method.answer: Functional Connectivity Integrative Normative Modelling (FUNCOIN), an adaptation of covariate-assisted principal regression.
nm2_modeling_method.reason: The paper explicitly names the modeling method 'FUNCOIN' and states that it is an adaptation of a recently developed statistical method.
nm2_modeling_method.supporting_text: FUNCOIN is an adaptation of a recently developed method from statistics literature, covariate-assisted principal regression...

nm3_software_tool.reason: The authors state they have released a specific Python package named 'FUNCOIN' to implement the described method.
nm3_software_tool.supporting_text: With this paper, a python package, 'FUNCOIN', is released (https://github.com/kobbersmed/funcoin), installable directly from GitHub or with pip.

nm4_response_variable.supporting_text: Our measure of brain function is FC, determined in this case as the Pearson correlation matrix from all pairs of the parcellation components (Fig. 1A, bottom).

The authors also explicitly checked for site effects, a key nuisance variable, and found them to be non-significant, so they were not included in the final model.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: The study compared the proportion of outliers (defined by Z-scores from the FUNCOIN model, with |z|>2) between healthy controls and patient groups (PD, BD) using permutation testing based on Fisher's exact test, with FDR correction. For comparison, it also evaluated edgewise models, summarizing Z-scores by counting outliers (analyzed with Mann-Whitney U tests) and by analyzing robust means of extreme Z-scores with an extreme value distribution.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: The novel whole-brain normative model (FUNCOIN) significantly identified individuals with Parkinson's disease (even years before diagnosis) and Bipolar disorder as outliers, while conventional edgewise models failed to do so.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Using a whole-brain normative model (FUNCOIN) on rsfMRI data from 46,000 controls, the study found a significantly higher proportion of outliers in patient groups compared to healthy controls. Specifically, 9.1% of Parkinson's disease (PD) patients had Z-scores < -2 in the first model component (p_adj=0.002), an effect that was also present in 9.3% of pre-diagnostic scans (up to 7.8 years prior, p_adj=0.01). Bipolar disorder (BD) subjects showed two distinct deviation patterns, with 7.9% having Z > 2 in component 1 and 6.9% having Z < -2 in component 2 (p_adj=0.046). In contrast, standard edgewise models and methods summarizing their Z-scores failed to robustly identify outlier individuals after correcting for multiple comparisons.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Z-score interpretation is challenging (direction of change is unknown a priori); clinical relevance of a deviation is hard to determine (could be artifact or chance); some patients may not be outliers if pathology moves them within the normal range. The model also only considers linear effects.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: As in other normative modelling studies of FC, interpretation of the Z -scores can be challenging. First, we do not know a priori whether given brain pathology increases or decreases Z -scores. Second, given an outlier from the normative model it is important but difficult to determine whether the subject's deviation from normal is clinically relevant (e.g. brain disease) or not (e.g. artifact or chance). Third, some subjects with brain disease may be unidentifiable by a normative model... Further, we only consider linear effects on FC.
caa10_key_limitations.location: Kobbersmed2025.pdf.md: Discussion / Limitations of our study

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The FUNCOIN model appeared to identify two distinct subgroups of Bipolar Disorder based on their different, non-overlapping patterns of deviation in the two model components (Z1>2 or Z2<-2), suggesting a potential for subtyping heterogeneous diseases.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study introduces a novel method, FUNCOIN, which is a bias-corrected adaptation of 'covariate-assisted principal regression'. The authors have released a Python package for this method. A key finding is the model's ability to detect abnormalities in Parkinson's disease patients up to 7.8 years before their formal diagnosis. The paper makes a strong argument for the superiority of integrative, whole-brain models over edgewise approaches for analyzing functional connectivity in the context of normative modeling.
